questions.question: Describe the relationship between the autonomic nervous system and the stress response.
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the relationship between the autonomic nervous system and the stress
  • response.
  • The autonomic nervous system (ANS) plays a key role in the body's stress response by
  • activating the sympathetic nervous system (SNS) and deactivating the parasympathetic
  • nervous system (PSNS):
  • Sympathetic nervous system: This system activates the body's "fight-or-flight" response,
  • Parasympathetic nervous system: This system is responsible for resting.

questions.question: Explain how neurotransmitters are involved in communication between neurons.
questions.solution_html:
• Explainhowneurotransmittersareinvolvedincommunicationbetweenneurons.
  • Neurotransmitters are the chemical messengers that transmit signals from one neuron to
  • another, or from neurons to target cells such as muscle cells or other types of neurons.
  • Neurotransmitters are released from the axon terminals of one neuron into the synapse,
  • which is the small gap between the sending neuron (presynaptic neuron) and the receiving
  • neuron (postsynaptic neuron). This release occurs in response to an electrical impulse
  • (action potential) in the presynaptic neuron.

questions.question: Describe the blood-brain barrier and its function.

  • The blood–brain barrier is playing a critical role in controlling the influx and efflux of
  • biological substances essential for the brain’s metabolic activity as well as neuronal
  • function. BBB maintains the homeostasis of the brain and neuronal functions, defending

questions.question: Differentiate between short-term and long-term potentiation. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:

  • ● A brief increase in synaptic strength lasting seconds to minutes, mainly due to
  • increased neurotransmitter release.
  • ● Long-Term Potentiation (LTP):
  • ● A long-lasting enhancement of synaptic strength lasting hours to years, involving protein
  • synthesis and formation of new receptors/synapses, important for memory.

questions.question: Describe the physiologic changes happen during the stimulation of symapathetic fibres. / [CO3, CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the physiologic changes happening during stimulation of sympathetic
  • fibres. [U]/[CO3,CO4]
  • Stimulation of sympathetic fibres produces the “fight-or-flight” response, causing:
  • ● Increased heart rate and blood pressure
  • ● Bronchodilation (more airflow to lungs)
  • ● Pupil dilation
  • ● Increased blood glucose due to glycogen breakdown
  • ● Reduced digestion (decreased gut motility and secretions)
  • ● Increased sweating and alertness (Mention flight or fight response and any three

  • The meninges are three protective layers surrounding the brain:
  • ● Dura mater – the tough, outermost layer.
  • ● Arachnoid mater – the middle, web-like layer.
  • ● Pia mater – the thin, delicate inner layer that closely covers the brain surface.
  • Function:
  • ● Protect the brain from injury.
  • ● Enclose and support blood vessels.
  • ● Contain cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) in the subarachnoid space, which cushions the brain
  • and maintains chemical stability. (Explanation of structures: 1 mark, Any two function:

questions.question: Discuss the Na+/K+ pump and its role in maintaining the resting membrane potential
questions.solution_html:
• DiscusstheNa+/K+pumpanditsroleinmaintainingtherestingmembranepotential
  • [2]
  • Definition of Na+/K+ pump.
  • Function: Actively transports 3 Na⁺ out and 2 K⁺ in against their concentration gradients using ATP.
  • Electrogenic Nature: Creates a net negative charge inside the cell by removing more positive ions
  • than it brings in.
  • Maintains Ion Gradients: Ensures high extracellular Na⁺ and high intracellular K⁺, critical for
  • membrane potential stability.
  • Supports Resting Potential: The pump helps maintain the resting membrane potential (~-70 mV) by
  • counteracting ion leaks, especially K⁺.
  • Action Potentials: Establishes ion gradients essential for nerve signaling and muscle contraction.

questions.question: Explain the role of the spinal cord in reflex action. / [CO3, CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the role of the spinal cord in reflex action. [U]/[CO3,CO4]
  • ● The spinal cord acts as the reflex center of the body.
  • ● Reflex actions are automatic, rapid, and involuntary responses to stimuli.
  • ● Sensory neurons carry signals from receptors to the spinal cord.
  • ● The spinal cord processes the information without sending it to the brain.
  • ● Motor neurons then carry the response from the spinal cord to the muscles or glands.
  • ● This quick pathway is called a reflex arc.
  • ● It helps protect the body by allowing immediate responses to danger (e.g., withdrawing
  • hand from fire). (Give full marks for a good account)
